title: Origins of the war — NZHistory
provider: Manatū Taonga — Ministry for Culture and Heritage
text: First World War chronology: Franz Ferdinand was assassinated on 28 June 1914. Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July. Russia ordered partial mobilisation the following day. Germany declared war on Russia on 1 August and France on 3 August. Germany’s invasion of Belgium prompted Britain’s declaration of war on 4 August. Nationalism, imperial rivalries, alliances and military planning contributed to escalation. The Triple Entente was an informal coalition, established in 1907, not a single automatic mutual-defence treaty.
locator: NZHistory, Origins of the war, updated 17 May 2017; concise paraphrase checked 15 October 2026
